title: MUSA attention set
purpose: The attention family of the MUSA operator evaluation: every KernelBench attention problem, the A-tier answer that already exists for it, the measurement that already exists for it, and what is still missing for each target.

origin_commits.c6b6eb0: add MUSA attention kernels for KernelBench level3 problems
origin_commits.898244a: tune MUSA attention kernels with tiled bands (43/44/50/31/97)
origin_commits.edee502: rewrite p97 SDPA as two register-tiled SGEMMs
origin_commits.60d82eb: rewrite p30 window attention as one CTA per (window, head)

warp_size_note: mp_22 (S4000) and mp_21 (S80) use 128-thread warps; mp_31 (S5000) uses 32. Every tuned A-tier kernel in this set was tuned on mp_22, and the tuning record shows the optimum sitting at the 1024-thread CTA ceiling with 32 lanes per query row. Those two facts are warp-size sensitive, so no mp_22 launch configuration should be carried to mp_31 without re-measuring. Source: docs/musa/README.md and docs/musa_attention_tuning_notes.md.
kernel_candidates_note: Candidate attention kernel implementations, one record per implementation. The detail, including upstream locations, lives in the sources record because that is where this repository keeps provenance; the index renders only what a reader needs to pick a candidate.

entries.structure: plain F.scaled_dot_product_attention over already-split Q/K/V, no mask, no GQA
entries.shape_note: head_dim 1024 is what rules out the flash-tile design here: the q/o state alone is about 8KB per row, so the band width collapses to at most 8 rows and latency starvation beats the bandwidth saved.

B_library.basis: torch_musa registers sdpa and routes it to muDNN SDP; mutlass experimental/fmha and MATE are the fused candidates

notes: The tuning record shows this problem spent many rounds far behind: 38176ms, then 3712ms after fixing uncoalesced access, then 1151ms after row-band K/V reuse, then 191ms once the two-stage register-tiled SGEMM replaced the flash-tile attempt.
This is the same shape family as the B-tier sdpa_forward_pilot task, so its trace and dispatch contract can be reused verbatim.

entries.structure: fused QKV linear, split into heads, scaled QK^T, top-left causal masked_fill(-inf), softmax, P.V, output projection

B_library.basis: the attention core is an sdpa call; the surrounding projections are nn.Linear and so are library-routed already
B_library.expected_path: fused_library for the core, library_composition for the projections

notes: The tuned kernel is a flash-tile band: FMHA_TILE_BM 32, FMHA_TILE_BN 32, 32 lanes per query row, 1024 threads per CTA, shared arrays padded by one element to break bank conflicts.
The intermediate band version was 1561ms and the first flash-tile attempt at BM16/BN32 was slower still (668ms core-only), so the thread count and tile size here are measured optima, not defaults.

entries.structure: a full MiniGPT transformer block: the causal attention of 43 plus the MLP and both residual paths

B_library.basis: same attention core as 43, but a much larger share of the runtime is now the library-routed MLP, which is exactly the composition case the tiers must separate

notes: Shares the kernel source with 43; the higher final ratio reflects the MLP share of the block rather than a better attention kernel.

entries.structure: causal self-attention with relu on the masked scores instead of softmax, so there is no denominator

B_library.reason: no fused library provides relu attention; the only library path would be a composition that materializes scores, which is the thing being measured

notes: Because there is no softmax denominator, the relu variant is a pure streaming weighted sum and needs no online rescale; the same kernel handles both modes.

entries.structure: single dense multi-head attention over a flattened 128x128 image, no mask, no causal
entries.shape_note: 16384 tokens at head_dim 32 is the long-sequence small-head case: the score matrix is quadratic in 16384 while the per-row state is tiny.

B_library.basis: a plain unmasked attention over a contiguous 4D tensor is what the fused library path is for

notes: The final design abandons flash-tile entirely and materializes S/P through a two-stage GEMM plus a global row softmax. On a dense long-sequence small-head problem the extra 8.6GB of intermediates costs less than the low arithmetic intensity of streaming rescale.
Shared memory budget scales as band x head_dim, so the BM128 configuration that won here fails outright at head_dim 96. A launch configuration is only valid for the head_dim it was measured on.

entries.structure: shifted-window attention with relative position bias over 7x7=49-token windows
entries.shape_note: The window is 49 tokens, which is smaller than one warp's worth of work at mp_22, so the parallel decomposition is the whole problem.

B_library.basis: window attention is still an attention core once the windows are gathered, so the dispatch question is whether to gather-then-call the fused path or stay in a custom window kernel

notes: The per-row kernel recomputed the whole window of K/V for every query row; one CTA per (window, head) that stages the entire window once cut the attention portion from 52ms to 18.5ms.
This is the closest entry to parity in the set at 0.81x, and the remaining gap is attributed to the serial per-row softmax inside the window kernel.

entries.structure: a 6-layer ViT whose per-layer attention is dense over 197 tokens at head_dim 64
entries.shape_note: Listed as degenerate in the tuning record: the attention core is not the bottleneck at this sequence length, and the kernels were left unchanged.

A_kernel.reason: the attention core is already inside the noise floor of the surrounding layers, so a kernel-level score would not measure kernel quality

B_library.reason: same reason: no dispatch decision here is worth more than the measurement noise

notes: Kept in the set as a control: an entry that is already at or above parity, to show what a degenerate case looks like in the report.

entries.structure: CvT whose attention operates on a small token count after convolutional token embedding
entries.shape_note: Degenerate like 28; the sequence is small and the convolution dominates.

A_kernel.reason: attention is not a meaningful share of the runtime

notes: Second control entry, already above parity.

related_problem_families.what_it_is: Twenty end-to-end HuggingFace causal language models driven through AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained: gpt2, gpt-neo-2.7B, opt-1.3b, bart-large, bigbird-roberta-base, electra-small, reformer-enwik8, at sequence lengths of 32 up to 4095.
related_problem_families.why_not_entries_here: These are whole-model forwards, not attention kernels. Scoring them would measure the whole graph, and the attention core is one contributor among many that the problem does not isolate.
related_problem_families.why_recorded: They are where the attention lengths and head counts that matter in production actually live: seq 4095 and 2047 shapes do not appear anywhere in this set's entries, and every one of them runs a real attention path. They are the natural A-tier targets if the question shifts from 'is the attention kernel good' to 'is the model fast', and they need transformers plus model weights, so they were out of scope for a no-hardware pass.

related_problem_families.what_it_is: Ten problems whose op chain contains softmax but no attention: for example ConvTranspose3d_Mean_Add_Softmax_Tanh_Scaling, Matmul_Dropout_Softmax, Gemm_BatchNorm_Scaling_Softmax.
related_problem_families.why_not_entries_here: Softmax over a channel axis in a conv chain is not attention. Grouping them in would inflate the attention set with problems whose bottleneck is the convolution.
related_problem_families.why_recorded: A softmax-shape search over level2 is how these get mistaken for attention problems, and they were in the initial filename sweep for exactly that reason. Recording the decision here keeps the next sweep from repeating it.
